name: Bo
confidence_why: The only statement about Bo stress is a hedged remark in Conrad and Dye's 1975 Upper Sepik survey that contrastive word stress was noted in Ama and "possibly" in Bo, with no Bo examples and word lists that carry no stress marks, while Laycock 1973 and 1975 say nothing about it, so the type of system remains unknown.
catalog_citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. Canberra: Australian National University.
catalog_locator: p.10, section 3.1 Arai Language Family, Figure C 'Summary of Arai Phonology', paragraph following the Nimo vowel examples
catalog_quote: Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga. Examples from Ama are: i'wa water / 'iwa leaf; a'mu moon / 'amu nose; mʌ'l̆a path / 'mʌl̆a vine. Syllable types CV, V and VV were found, with closed syllables only in Bo and consonant clusters only in Nimo and Owiniga.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (Conrad & Dye 1975, PL A-40), rendered p.10 (= printed p.10) as an image and read. Under 'Figure C Summary of Arai Phonology' the passage reads exactly: 'Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga. Examples from Ama are: i'wa water / 'iwa leaf; a'mu moon / 'amu nose; mʌ'l̆a path / 'mʌl̆a vine. Syllable types CV, V and VV were found, with closed syllables only in Bo and consonant clusters only in Nimo and Owiniga.' The only difference from the compilers quote is the flap diacritic on the l in the Ama path/vine pair (reporter wrote mʌ'la / 'mʌla); the Bo sentence itself is verbatim. Surrounding section (3.1 Arai Language Family, pp.8-11…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-level statement only: the authors tentatively ('possibly') report contrastive (i.e. lexically distinctive, not positionally fixed) word stress in Bo, by analogy with the minimal pairs they recorded for Ama; no Bo examples, no default position, and the Bo wordlist forms (Table 2, pp.20-24) are printed without stress marks. If taken at face value the reading would be lexical (unpredictable), but the hedge makes it unresolved.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement itself is hedged ('possibly').
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('word stress'), based on elicited survey wordlist items (citation forms) collected 1963-1973; family-level phonology summary, not a description of Bo as such.
new_statements.identity_note: Conrad & Dye's 'Bo' = villages Bo, Kobaru, Kaumifi, Nigyama, Umarita in the West Range (p.9), i.e. the same unit as Ethnologue/Glottolog Bo bpw/bopa1235 (dialects Kaboru, Nikiyama, Umuruta); Laycock 1973 lists it as entry 169 'Po' (villages Sori = Nigyama, Umirita). The stress remark is a family-level (Arai/Left May) summary in which Bo is named only as 'possibly' sharing Ama's contrastive stress.
